correctness.rationale: Exact Fourier fourth moment has two resonances. The stationary cubic has one simple positive root for all squared radii in (0,1). The transverse coefficient sign is that of R_s(x_s); its resultant is 54 s^6 Q(s) E(s), where E is strictly positive. Exact Sturm isolations and first subresultant sign certificates distinguish the physical positive root at s_c from a negative branch at the second algebraic root. The trace bound H/(2 A*) <= 2s(1+s^2) < 1 for s <= 2/5 gives the global regime. All identities and Sturm checks were replayed from the new standalone checker.
